title: Civil Engineering Materials
topics: Quality control and testing of materials

items.q: A mix needs 300 kg of cement per cubic metre. How many 50 kg bags is that?
An aggregate sample of mass 1500 kg fills a container of volume 0.02 m3. Find its bulk density in kg/m3.
items.s: Bulk density = 1500/0.02 = 75000 kg/m3.

items.q: A 1 : 4 cement sand mortar is to be made with 75 kg of cement. How much sand is needed, in kg?
items.s: Sand = 4 x cement = 4 x 75 = 300 kg.

items.q: For 300 kg of cement and a water cement ratio of 0.55, find the mass of water required in kg.
items.s: Water = w/c x cement = 0.55 x 300 = 165 kg.

items.q: A mix of water cement ratio 0.5 uses 180 kg of water per m3. Find the cement content in kg.
items.s: Cement = water/(w/c) = 180/0.5 = 360 kg.

items.q: A concrete cube 100 mm square fails at a load of 500 kN. Calculate its compressive strength in N/mm2.
items.s: Strength = load/area = 500000/(100 x 100) = 50 N/mm2.
items.t: Quality control and testing of materials

items.q: In a compaction factor test the partially compacted concrete has mass 12.8 kg and the fully compacted mass is 14.0 kg. Find the compaction factor.
items.s: Compaction factor = 12.8/14.0 = 0.9143.
items.t: Quality control and testing of materials

items.q: A concrete specimen of volume 0.25 m3 has a mass of 2400 kg. Calculate its density in kg/m3.

A standard slump cone 300 mm high is lifted and the concrete settles to a height of 195 mm. Calculate the true slump in mm.
items.s: True slump = 300 - 195 = 105 mm.

items.q: Sieve analysis gives cumulative percentages retained of 4, 12, 28, 58, 82, 94 on successive sieves. Calculate the fineness modulus.
items.s: Fineness modulus = sum of cumulative % retained/100 = 278/100 = 2.78.

items.q: An aggregate sample has oven dry mass 750 g, saturated surface dry mass 768 g and apparent mass in water 312 g. Find its bulk specific gravity.
items.s: Bulk SG = dry mass/(SSD - submerged) = 750/(768 - 312) = 1.64 = 1.65.

items.q: An aggregate of oven dry mass 800 g takes up water to reach a saturated surface dry mass of 824 g. Calculate the water absorption in percent.
items.s: Absorption = (SSD - dry)/dry x 100 = (824 - 800)/800 x 100 = 3%.

items.q: Soundness of cement may be defined as
o: a concrete mix whose proportions are chosen from target strength and workability requirements
an aggregate that reacts harmfully with alkalis in cement, causing expansion
the chemical attack of a metal by its environment, producing rust on steel in moist air
the ability of set cement to retain its volume without disruptive expansion
items.s: Soundness of cement: the ability of set cement to retain its volume without disruptive expansion. The other options describe Corrosion, Reactive aggregate, Design mix.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Proof stress.
o: a concrete mix whose proportions are chosen from target strength and workability requirements

the hydraulic binder made by burning and grinding limestone and clay, which sets under water
the stress that produces a stated small permanent strain in a metal without a clear yield point
items.s: Proof stress: the stress that produces a stated small permanent strain in a metal without a clear yield point. The other options describe Design mix, Portland cement, Ductility.

items.s: Burnt clay brick: a masonry unit shaped from clay and fired to give strength and durability. The other options describe Honeycombing, Water absorption, Galvanising.

items.q: An aggregate sample has oven dry mass 600 g, saturated surface dry mass 615 g and apparent mass in water 375 g. Find its bulk specific gravity.
items.s: Bulk SG = dry mass/(SSD - submerged) = 600/(615 - 375) = 2.5.
